cases.name: Sharon Hensley
cases.about:
About 60 friends and family members gathered for her memorial in 2016 remembered her as a fun-loving dancer, model, classmate and sister. “She was very free-spirited,” recalled her friend, Diane Binder. “She always had a smile on her face, and she was happy — that’s Sharon.”

https://www.clarionledger.com/story/news/2016/08/30/long-goodbye-sharon-hensley-felix-vail-jerry-mitchell/89586312/

In 1967, Sharon discovered she was pregnant. Wanting to escape her hometown, she followed her brother Frank and other classmates to San Francisco, where thousands of other young people were already gathering for the “summer of love.”
“She believed in love,” Brian recalled. “She believed in happiness. She believed in flowers and beads.” After arriving in the Bay area, she stayed in a home for unwed mothers, where she gave birth to a girl she named “Cherry” after the popular Neil Diamond song. She told friends she wanted to keep the child, but was unable to.

In New Orleans, Sharon Hensley worked as a table dancer at a strip club. IN Miami, where she and Vail lived in a commune and worked at a health food store.
